newsitem.title: SPAIN: Two suspects sought in ETA killing - Spain radio.
newsitem.headline: Two suspects sought in ETA killing - Spain radio.

text.p: At least two of the suspected Basque separatist rebels who fled their hideout after an explosion on Thursday were under investigation for possible links to a killing that caused a national outcry, state radio reported.

In the first sign of progress in the search for the killers of politician Miguel Angel Blanco, state radio cited unnamed sources saying the suspects were among four people being sought after a blast tore through an apartment in the Basque town of Durango.
The two fugitives had been under scrutiny for possible involvement in Blanco's kidnapping last Thursday as well his murder last weekend, the radio station reported.
Blanco's death ignited massive street protests against the ETA separatist group that kidnapped him.

The explosion in the Durango apartment led to the discovery of a guerrilla "safe house" packed with weapons, bomb parts and detonators, authorities said. The blast was believed to have been caused by a grenade that went off by accident.
Police blanketed the area and set up roadblocks in an effort to catch the four alleged ETA members who fled the hideout.
Spanish officials had said earlier it was too soon to tell whether the suspects had any connection to Blanco's killing.

ETA rebels who kidnapped Blanco -- a 29-year-old Basque town councillor -- had threatened to execute him unless the government gave in to their demands within 48 hours. The government refused, and the rebels shot him twice in the head. He died early on Sunday.
